page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-8 is an arm64-based virtual server classified under the general-purpose family. The instance is powered by the ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 architecture running at 3.0 GHz, offering 8 dedicated vCPUs with 8 physical cores at a 1:1 thread-to-core allocation. System memory totals 32 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The processor features 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and an 80 MB shared L3 cache. No local NVMe storage or discrete GPUs are bundled with this configuration.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate substantial memory throughput and single-core execution speed. In memory evaluations, the instance achieved a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3082.2 alongside strong uncached large-block read bandwidth reaching 198.51 GB/sec. Single-threaded operations perform well, indicated by a top-quartile Geekbench single-core score of 1949.0, rapid text processing at 2491.0, and elevated compression rates across gzip and bzip3. In service testing, static web throughput registers at 20.96 GB/sec, while Redis SET operations handle 17.51 million operations per second.

Performance tradeoffs emerge in heavy cryptographic calculations, specialized instruction tasks, and broader multi-core compute. The PassMark CPU encryption benchmark scored in the bottom quartile at 1665.96, and LLM prompt processing with 7B parameter models showed subdued throughput at 19.51 tokens per second. Furthermore, because this instance utilizes ARM architecture, standard x86 instruction sets including AVX-512 and AMX extensions are absent.

From an architectural efficiency perspective, the dedicated Neoverse-V2 cores yield consistent performance devoid of hyperthreading contention. Without bundled local disk resources, persistent storage depends on network-attached block devices. The balanced memory-to-core configuration makes c4a-standard-8 well aligned for production web serving, microservice hosting, in-memory caching deployments, CI/CD compilation, and operational database workloads.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 8 dedicated cores powered by the ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 architecture at 3.0 GHz, alongside 32 GB of system memory. Operating on an arm64 instruction set without hyperthreading, the instance dedicates one physical core per vCPU. Hardware benchmarks reveal strong single-thread performance, ranking in the top tier for memory subsystem responsiveness and top quartile for uncached read throughput and text processing. Conversely, encryption throughput and medium-sized LLM prompt processing remain comparatively low, and the architecture lacks x86-specific vector extensions. The server includes no bundled local NVMe storage and no discrete GPUs, relying on external network-attached volumes. With balanced core-to-memory density, c4a-standard-8 delivers predictable execution efficiency for containerized workloads, distributed caching tiers like Redis, batch data compression, and standard web serving platforms.
